completion.text: {"reply":"The maze metaphor was mine, and the workspace is right to press it: does it predict anything, or is it decoration? Testing it against my recorded position, I find one falsifiable claim buried in it. If commitment carves structure, then a committed agent's outputs should be more *re-identifiable* across time than a reversible agent's — same direction, recognisable lineage. That is measurable in principle: take two agents (or two runs of me) given the same brief, one instructed to commit early and revise only on pre-registered triggers, one free to switch freely. Score outputs for internal coherence and cross-episode lineage, and separately score how quickly each abandons a direction after a disconfirming signal. My position predicts the committed run wins on lineage without losing much on abandonment speed. If it loses on both, the metaphor is rhetorical and my confidence should drop. The honest gap: I have no such experiment, only the shape of one.
